meta.note: Recipes and EXP from NiaMeowDB's crafting database (348 recipes, launch build). Drop sources are community-reported on NiaMeowDB, so treat them as good places to look, not exact rates.

Screw.made: Weaponcrafting Lv1: 1 Bronze Ingot + 1 Iron Ingot = 10 Screws (or 10 Iron Hog's Metal Hooves = 3)

basics: Crafting opens at level 10. Each profession starts with a quest from its mentor; any character can learn all six.
Crafting levels 2 to 8 need character level 5 × the crafting level (crafting 4 needs character 20, crafting 8 needs 40). Crafting is capped at level 8 at launch.
At your cap the bar sits at 100% and extra crafting EXP is thrown away, so stop crafting until your character catches up.
Refining is 5 to 1: five ore make one ingot (100 to 500 mesos per craft), ten Tree Branches make one Processed Wood, five Leather make one Processed Leather.
Professions feed each other: Smithing makes the ingots, Weaponcrafting turns ingots into Screws, Woodcrafting makes Processed Wood, Tailoring turns Animal Fur Bundles into thread.
Most recipes lose mesos at NPC prices. Craft for gear you can't buy, for the EXP, or for the Free Market.

professions.name: Smithing
professions.makes: Ingots, helmets, gloves, boots, shields and claws (Iron Knuckle). Every other metal recipe in the game starts here.
professions.goodFor: Warriors and Thieves, and anyone who wants to sell ingots
keep: Iron Ingots go into 22 Smithing recipes. The single most-used metal.
13 recipes, from Mithril Koif to Mithril Tower Shield.
8 recipes, mostly level 5+ helms and boots.
Bronze Ingots, and half of every Screw.
Processed Leather for gloves and boots (8 recipes).
Adamantium Tower Shield and Knuckle at level 8.
Orihalcon Burgonet Helm, Missel and Jangoon Shoes.
Silver War Boots and Battle Grieves.
Blood Battle Grieves, Great Red Helmet.
professions.tip: Smithing uses about 370 Screws across its recipes, and Screws come from Weaponcrafting. Learn both, or keep Bronze and Iron Ore to trade for Screws.
professions.bases: Many recipes upgrade a basic helmet you already own (Bronze Koif, Bronze Helmet, Bronze Viking Helm, Steel Sharp Helm). Keep those drops instead of selling them.
professions.money: Iron Knuckle (level 8) is one of the few crafts that makes mesos at NPC prices, about +1.5k each.

professions.name: Weaponcrafting
professions.makes: Warrior and Thief weapons (Gephart, Sabretooth, Titan, Steel Guards) and Screws.
professions.goodFor: Warriors, Thieves, and anyone who needs Screws
keep: Iron Ingots go into 25 of 34 recipes.
Bronze Ingot + Iron Ingot = 10 Screws. You'll need hundreds.
Processed Leather: about 240 across the claw recipes (Titans, Igor, Guards).
Processed Wood for 11 recipes (shovels, polearms, mops).
7 recipes including Gephart and Halfmoon Zamadar.
10 hooves = 3 Screws, a backup Screw source.
professions.tip: Make Screws early (level 1 recipe) and keep a stack. Smithing, Tailoring, Woodcrafting and Leatherworking all eat them.
professions.bases: Higher tiers upgrade a weapon you craft first (Steel Titans → Mithril or Gold Titans, Bronze Igor → Steel or Adamantium Igor). Don't sell the base.
professions.money: Every Weaponcrafting recipe loses mesos at NPC prices. Craft it for the weapons, not the money.

professions.name: Tailoring
professions.makes: Hats, overalls, robes, shoes and capes (Lutia, Noel, Justice Cape). Mostly Magician gear.
professions.goodFor: Magicians, and anyone who wants cheap hats and capes
keep: 10 = 1 Processed Cloth. Cloth is in 47 of 51 recipes.
5 = 1 Processed Cloth, or 1 = 10 Spool of Thread (thread is in 33 recipes).
8 recipes: Blood Mesana, Red Lutia, Red Noel and more.
Blue Lutia, Blue Noel, Blue Justice Cape.
10 for the Red Bandana and Red Apprentice Hat.
10 for the Blue Bandana and Blue Apprentice Hat.
10 for the Brown Apprentice Hat and Ghetto Beanie.
professions.tip: The cheapest start in the game: Bandanas and Apprentice Hats use snail shells and mushroom caps you get from Maple Island and early Victoria. Dyes are sold by NPCs.
professions.money: Almost every Tailoring recipe loses mesos at NPC prices, but hats and capes sell to players.

professions.name: Woodcrafting
professions.makes: Bows, crossbows, wands, staffs, wooden weapons, chairs and arrows. Bows aren't sold in shops in Classic, so Bowmen live here.
professions.goodFor: Bowmen (almost every bow is crafted), Magicians, and leveling any profession cheaply
keep: 10 = 1 Processed Wood. Wood is in 28 of 36 recipes.
One per 500 arrows. Bowmen burn through these.
Bronze Arrows (level 4) need a Bronze Ingot per 500.
Iron Arrows (level 7) and Composite, Battle and Mountain bows.
Battle Bow, Mountain Crossbow, Ryden, Eagle Crow.
30 for the Hardwood Wand, which makes about +700 mesos per craft.
professions.tip: The cheapest profession to level: Wooden Sword and Wand (level 2), then Wooden Baseball Bat (level 3) and Balanche (level 4) cost almost nothing per EXP.
professions.money: Most profit-positive recipes live here: Iron Arrows ×500 (about +880 each), Hardwood Wand (about +710).

professions.name: Leatherworking
professions.makes: Gloves, shoes, hats and Thief/Bowman armor (Diros, Savata, Wolfskin, Sylvia, Braces). The biggest recipe book: 74 recipes.
professions.goodFor: Thieves and Bowmen, and anyone who wants gloves
keep: 5 = 1 Processed Leather. Leather is in 71 of 74 recipes, about 400 total.
Spool of Thread: about 600 across the recipes.
10 = 1 Processed Leather (level 4), plus Green Jack and Lappy Boots.
Blue Diros, Savata, Lappy and Hunter Boots.
Black Duo, Dark Mischief, Dark Wolfskin, Black Lappy Boots.
Basic Archer Gloves and Blue Duo.
Three level 8 recipes, 120 skulls in total.
professions.tip: Leather is the bottleneck. Fire Boars, Ribbon Pigs, Pigs and Wild Boars all drop it, and it sells fast on the Free Market, so decide early whether you're crafting or selling.
professions.money: Every Leatherworking recipe loses mesos at NPC prices. Gloves still sell well because they only come from drops, quests and crafting.

professions.name: Arcforge
professions.makes: Cut gems from ore, Lesser scrolls (hat, top, bottom, shoes, shield, cape, earring), Magician wands and staffs, and the Fairy Wand.
professions.goodFor: Magicians (wands and staffs), and anyone who wants to make their own scrolls
keep: 10 per scroll. About 180 across the scroll recipes.
3 Leather = 1 Processed Parchment, one per scroll.
HP scrolls, Wizard Wand, Fairy Wand.
MP scrolls and the Emerald Staff.
DEF scrolls and the Fairy Wand (cut at level 6).
Earring stat scrolls (level 8). Cut Black Crystal also makes about +800 mesos.
Cape Magic DEF scroll, Sapphire Staff, Fairy Wand.
Ice Wand, Mithril Wand, Wizard Wand.
professions.tip: Arcforge is the gem cutter: ore → gem costs 200 to 1,200 mesos per gem, and every other profession needs gems. Scrolls are pricey (10k-20k mesos each) but give big EXP.
professions.money: Cutting Black Crystal (level 6) is profit-positive at about +800 per craft.

faq: What is the best crafting profession in MapleStory Classic?

It depends on your class. Bowmen need Woodcrafting because bows aren't sold in shops. Warriors and Thieves get the most from Smithing plus Weaponcrafting. Magicians get wands from Arcforge and robes from Tailoring. For pure leveling, Woodcrafting is the cheapest.
Can you learn every crafting profession?
Yes. Any character can learn all six once they reach level 10, by doing each mentor's starter quest.
What is the max crafting level in Classic?
Level 8 at launch. Each crafting level from 2 to 8 needs your character to be 5× that level, so crafting 8 needs character level 40.
What items should I not sell in MapleStory Classic?
Ores (especially Iron, Mithril, Bronze and Gold), Leather, Animal Fur Bundles, Screws and gem ores are used by the most recipes. Snail shells and mushroom caps are needed for early hats.
How do I get Screws in MapleStory Classic?
Weaponcrafting level 1: one Bronze Ingot plus one Iron Ingot makes 10 Screws. At level 5 you can also turn 10 Iron Hog's Metal Hooves into 3 Screws.
